outcome: Maternal outcome (oxytocin given, perineal laceration, type of episiotomy, size of episiotomy, mode of delivery, fatigue)
Neonatal outcome (crown heel length, head circumference, neonate resuscitation, NICU admission, APGAR score)
cohort: The study included 60 primigravida mothers admitted to selected hospitals in Pune city, India.
finding: The Valsalva bearing down technique resulted in significantly better maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to the spontaneous bearing down technique, which had negative effects.
mod_finding: The mode of delivery was found to be significantly different between the Valsalva and spontaneous bearing down techniques, with Valsalva leading to better outcomes.
cross-section timing: Observations were made during the second stage of labor and immediately postpartum.
